# Introduction

I wondered if there was some software that would allow to manage data files with the same ease (ease...) that Git provides for managing code files.

My quest quickly led me to find DVC, which stands for "Data Version Control". The project website can be found at <https://dvc.org/>, and the GitHub repository is at <https://github.com/iterative/dvc>.

I gave it a go through a mini project, thus learning the basic workflow of DVC. In this post, I will try to explain what I actually did. I hope this can serve as a quick kickstart reference for anyone who wants to get learn DVC.

# Goals of the mini-project

I am planning on reading and **editing** a few pdf books in the upcoming months. A natural idea to save my progress would be a versioning system, but since pdfs are binary files, I cannot use barebone Git for this, and this is where DVC makes its entrance.

# Methodology

DVC is a command line tool just like git, and it is meant to be used alongside git according to a "workflow". The workflow is as follows:

1. As usual, we first create our working directory, which I'll call `education`, and we git initialize it:

    ```bash
    mkdir ~/education
    cd ~/education
    git init .
    ```

2. Then, we initialize DVC in our wokring directory, which looks just like we do in git:

    ```bash
    dvc init
    ```

3. Now, here is the idea behind managing data files with DVC:
    
    * say we have a data file `./book.pdf` that we want to manage with DVC. Instead of adding `./book.pdf` to git via our usual `git add ./book.pdf` command (like we would do with text files), we add it to DVC via a very look-alikey command: `dvc add ./book.pdf`.

    * This will create a new text file `./book.pdf.dvc` (right next to where `./book.pdf` is located) which will act as a "pointer" to the actual data file `./book.pdf`.
    
    * I say "pointer" because the `./book.pdf.dvc` file will contain a hash of the actual data file `./book.pdf`, thus "linking" or "pointing" to the latter uniquely.
    
    * Then, since the `./book.pdf.dvc` file is just a regular text file, we can add it to git via `git add ./book.pdf.dvc`, thus creating a commit that holds a light textual pointer that links to the heavy data file: `./book.pdf.dvc *> ./book.pdf`.

    * At the same time, the moment we do `dvc add ./book.pdf`, in addition to creating the pointer file 
    
    
The actual data file will be moved to a hidden directory `.dvc/cache` in the working directory, and the pointer file `./book.pdf.dvc` will be added to git instead of the actual data file.
    ```bash
    dvc add book.pdf
    ```
